questions.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}} & =\frac{A}{(x-2)}+\frac{B}{(x-2)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)^{2}$ and get

$$
4x=A(x-2)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2) & =A(2-2)+B \\ 8 & =0+B \\ B & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0) & =A(0-2)+B \\ 0 & =-2A+B \\ 0 & =-2A+8 \\ A & =\frac{8}{2} \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{4}{(x-2)}+\frac{8}{(x-2)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(\frac{4}{(x-2)}+\frac{8}{(x-2)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x+8{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|{|}_{3}^{4}+8(-\frac{1}{x-2}){|}_{3}^{4} \\  & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-2|)+8(-\frac{1}{4-2}+\frac{1}{3-2}) \\  & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-2|)+8(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2+4.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{x+1}{(x+5)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x+5}+\frac{B}{(x+5)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+5)^{2}$ and get

$$
x+1=A(x+5)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=-5,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5+1 & =A(-5+5)+B \\ B & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+1 & =A(0+5)-4 \\ 1 & =5A-4 \\ 5A & =5 \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{x+1}{(x+5)^{2}}=\frac{1}{x+5}-\frac{4}{(x+5)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x+1}{(x+5)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{x+5}-\frac{4}{(x+5)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x+5}\,\text{d}x-4{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+5)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+5|\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{4}{x+5}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+5|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0+5|)+(\frac{4}{1+5}-\frac{4}{0+5}) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡6-\operatorname{ln}⁡5)+(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{4}{5}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{6}{5})-\frac{2}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{x+2}{(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x-4}+\frac{B}{(x-4)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-4)^{2}$ and get

$$
x+2=A(x-4)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4+2 & =A(4-4)+B \\ B & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+2 & =A(0-4)+6 \\ 2 & =-4A+6 \\ 4A & =4 \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{x+2}{(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{1}{x-4}+\frac{6}{(x-4)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{x+2}{(x-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{1}{x-4}+\frac{6}{(x-4)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x+6{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|\,{|}_{1}^{2}-\frac{6}{x-4}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-4|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-4|)-(\frac{6}{2-4}-\frac{6}{1-4}) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-(-3-(-2)) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})+1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{4x-10}{(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{A}{(x-2)}+\frac{B}{(x-2)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)^{2}$ and get

$$
4x-10=A(x-2)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2)-10 & =A(2-2)+B \\ -2 & =0+B \\ B & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)-10 & =A(0-2)+B \\ -10 & =-2A-2 \\ -2A & =-8 \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{4x-10}{(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{4}{(x-2)}-\frac{2}{(x-2)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4x-10}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{4}{(x-2)}-\frac{2}{(x-2)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|-2(-\frac{1}{x-2})+C \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+\frac{2}{x-2}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+3 & =A(0-5)+8 \\ 3 & =-5A+8 \\ 5A & =5 \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{x+3}{(x-5)^{2}}=\frac{1}{x-5}+\frac{8}{(x-5)^{2}}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x+3}{(x-5)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{x-5}+\frac{8}{(x-5)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x-5}\,\text{d}x+8{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x-5)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-5|\,{|}_{0}^{1}-\frac{8}{x-5}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-5|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0-5|)-(\frac{8}{1-5}-\frac{8}{0-5}) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡5)-(-2-(-\frac{8}{5})) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{5})+\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{5x+35}{(x+2)^{2}(x-3)}=\frac{A}{(x+2)}+\frac{B}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-3)}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+2)^{2}(x-3)$ and get

$$
5x+35=A(x+2)(x-3)+B(x-3)+C(x+2)^{2}.
$$

Plugging in $x=-2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $C$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-2)+35 & =A(-2+2)(-2-3)+B(-2-3)+C(-2+2)^{2} \\ -10+35 & =B(-5) \\ B & =\frac{25}{-5} \\ B & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(3)+35 & =A(3+2)(3-3)+B(3-3)+C(3+2)^{2} \\ 15+35 & =C{(5)}^{2} \\ C & =\frac{50}{25} \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $B$ and $C,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(0)+35 & =A(0+2)(0-3)+B(0-3)+C(0+2)^{2} \\ 35 & =-6A-3B+4C \\ 35 & =-6A-3(-5)+4(2) \\ 35 & =-6A+23 \\ 6A & =-35+23 \\ A & =\frac{-12}{6} \\ A & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{5x+35}{(x+2)^{2}(x-3)}=-\frac{2}{(x+2)}-\frac{5}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-3)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x+35}{(x+2)^{2}(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{2}{(x+2)}-\frac{5}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-3)})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{(x+2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+\frac{5}{x+2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{14{x}^{2}+47x+42}{(2x+3)^{2}(x+3)}=\frac{A}{(2x+3)}+\frac{B}{(2x+3)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+3)}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(2x+3)^{2}(x+3)$ and get

$$
14{x}^{2}+47x+42=A(2x+3)(x+3)+B(x+3)+C(2x+3)^{2}.
$$

Plugging in $x=-\frac{3}{2},$ we can eliminate $A$ and $C$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}14{(-\frac{3}{2})}^{2}+47(-\frac{3}{2})+42 & =A(2(-\frac{3}{2})+3)(-\frac{3}{2}+3) \\  & +B(-\frac{3}{2}+3)+C{(2(-\frac{3}{2})+3)}^{2} \\ \frac{63}{2}-\frac{141}{2}+42 & =B(\frac{3}{2}) \\ \frac{63-141+84}{2} & =B(\frac{3}{2}) \\ B & =-\frac{12}{6} \\ B & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=-3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}14(-3)^{2}+47(-3)+42 & =A(2(-3)+3)(-3+3)+B(-3+3)+C(2(-3)+3)^{2} \\ 126-141+42 & =C{(-3)}^{2} \\ C & =\frac{27}{9} \\ C & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $B$ and $C,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}14({0}^{2})+47(0)+42 & =A(2(0)+3)(0+3)+B(0+3)+C(2(0)+3)^{2} \\ 42 & =9A+3B+9C \\ 42 & =9A+3(2)+9(3) \\ 42 & =9A+33 \\ 9A & =42-33 \\ A & =\frac{9}{9} \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{14{x}^{2}+47x+42}{(2x+3)^{2}(x+3)}=\frac{1}{(2x+3)}+\frac{2}{(2x+3)^{2}}+\frac{3}{(x+3)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{14{x}^{2}+47x+42}{(2x+3)^{2}(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{(2x+3)}+\frac{2}{(2x+3)^{2}}+\frac{3}{(x+3)})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{2x+3}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{(2x+3)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+3|-\frac{1}{2x+3}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{8-x}{x(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x-4}+\frac{C}{(x-4)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x(x-4)^{2}$ and get

$$
8-x=A(x-4)^{2}+Bx(x-4)+Cx.
$$

Plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and $C$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8-0 & =A(0-4)^{2}+B(0)(0-4)+C(0) \\ 8 & =16A \\ A & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8-4 & =A(4-4)^{2}+B(4)(4-4)+C(4) \\ 4 & =4C \\ C & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=1$ and substituting the known values of $A$ and $C,$ we can solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8-1 & =A(1-4)^{2}+B(1)(1-4)+C(1) \\ 7 & =9A-3B+C \\ 7 & =9(\frac{1}{2})-3B+1 \\ B & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{8-x}{x(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{1}{2x}-\frac{1}{2(x-4)}+\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}}
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{8-x}{x(x-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{1}{2x}-\frac{1}{2(x-4)}+\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|\,{|}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|\,{|}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{x-4}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}+\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{-9x+27}{(1-x)^{2}(x+5)}=\frac{A}{(1-x)}+\frac{B}{(1-x)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+5)}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(1-x)^{2}(x+5)$ and get

$$
-9x+27=A(1-x)(x+5)+B(x+5)+C(1-x)^{2}.
$$

Plugging in $x=1,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $C$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-9(1)+27 & =A(1-1)(1+5)+B(1+5)+C(1-1)^{2} \\ -9+27 & =B(6) \\ B & =\frac{18}{6} \\ B & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=-5,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-9(-5)+27 & =A(1-(-5))(-5+5)+B(-5+5)+C(1-(-5))^{2} \\ -45+27 & =C{(6)}^{2} \\ C & =\frac{72}{36} \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $B$ and $C,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-9(0)+27 & =A(1-0)(0+5)+B(0+5)+C(1-0)^{2} \\ 27 & =5A+5B+C \\ 27 & =5A+5(3)+2 \\ 27 & =5A+17 \\ 5A & =27-17 \\ A & =\frac{10}{5} \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{-9x+27}{(1-x)^{2}(x+5)}=\frac{2}{(1-x)}+\frac{3}{(1-x)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x+5)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-9x+27}{(1-x)^{2}(x+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{(1-x)}+\frac{3}{(1-x)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x+5)})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{1-x}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{(1-x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-x|+\frac{3}{1-x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+5|+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.

$$

$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2-0 & =A(0-6)-4 \\ 2 & =-6A-4 \\ A & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum:

$$
\frac{2-x}{(x-6)^{2}}=-\frac{1}{x-6}-\frac{4}{(x-6)^{2}}
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{2-x}{(x-6)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{5}(-\frac{1}{x-6}-\frac{4}{(x-6)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{x-6}\,\text{d}x-4{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{(x-6)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-6|\,{|}_{2}^{5}+4\cdot \frac{1}{x-6}\,{|}_{2}^{5} \\  & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡4)+4(-1-(-\frac{1}{4})) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4+4(-\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4-3.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{x(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x-2}+\frac{C}{(x-2)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x(x-2)^{2}$ and get

$$
4{x}^{2}-12x+4=A(x-2)^{2}+Bx(x-2)+Cx.
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2)^{2}-12(2)+4 & =A(2-2)^{2}+B(2)(2-2)+C(2) \\ -4 & =2C \\ C & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and $C$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}-12(0)+4 & =A(0-2)^{2}+B(0)(0-2)+C(0) \\ 4 & =4A \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=1$ and substituting the known values of $A$ and $C,$ we can solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(1)^{2}-12(1)+4 & =A(1-2)^{2}+B(1)(1-2)+C(1) \\ -4 & =A-B+C \\ -4 & =1-B+(-2) \\ -3 & =-B \\ B & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+4x}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2}{(x-2)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x}+\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2}{(x-2)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+\frac{2}{x-2}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
5{t}^{2}+20t+6=A(t+1)^{2}+B(t)(t+1)+C(t).
$$

Plugging in $t=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and $C$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(0)^{2}+20(0)+6 & =A(0+1)^{2}+B(0)(0+1)+C(0) \\ 6 & =A \\ A & =6\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-1)^{2}+20(-1)+6 & =A(-1+1)^{2}+B(-1)(-1+1)+C(-1) \\ -9 & =-C \\ C & =9\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(1)^{2}+20(1)+6 & =A(1+1)^{2}+B(1)(1+1)+C(1) \\ 31 & =4A+2B+C \\ 31 & =4(6)+2B+(9) \\ B & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{5{t}^{2}+20t+6}{t(t+1)^{2}}=\frac{6}{t}-\frac{1}{t+1}+\frac{9}{(t+1)^{2}}.

$$

$$

$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(2x+1)^{3}$ and get

$$
4{x}^{2}=A(2x+1)^{2}+B(2x+1)+C.
$$

Plugging in $x=-\frac{1}{2},$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$

$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2} & =A(2(0)+1)^{2}+B(2(0)+1)+C \\ 0 & =A+B+1 \\ A+B & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=-1$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(-1)^{2} & =A(2(-1)+1)^{2}+B(2(-1)+1)+C \\ 4 & =A-B+1 \\ A-B & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations $A-B=3$ and $A+B=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2A & =3-1 \\ A & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting back into $A+B=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1+B & =-1 \\ B & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum:

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}}{(2x+1)^{3}}=\frac{1}{2x+1}-\frac{2}{(2x+1)^{2}}+\frac{1}{(2x+1)^{3}}.
$$

$$

\dfrac{x}{(x+1)^2} = \dfrac {1}{x+1} - \dfrac {1}{(x+1)^2}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+2x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{x+1}-\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|{|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{1}{x+1}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+1|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0+1|)+(\frac{1}{1+1}-\frac{1}{0+1}) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)+(\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9{x}^{2}+2x-1}{(3x-1)^{3}} & =\frac{A}{(3x-1)}+\frac{B}{(3x-1)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(3x-1)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(3x-1)^3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}+2x-1 & =A(3x-1)^{2}+B(3x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=\dfrac{1}{3},$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}9{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+2(\frac{1}{3})-1 & =A{(3(\frac{1}{3})-1)}^{2}+B(3(\frac{1}{3})-1)+C \\ C & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}9{(0)}^{2}+2(0)-1 & =A{(0-1)}^{2}+B(0-1)+C \\ -1 & =A-B+\frac{2}{3} \\ A-B & =-\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=1$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get another equation relating $A$ and $B\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}9{(1)}^{2}+2(1)-1 & =A{(3(1)-1)}^{2}+B(3(1)-1)+C \\ 10 & =4A+2B+\frac{2}{3} \\ 2A+B & =\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding our two equations $A-B=-\dfrac{5}{3}$ and $2A+B=\dfrac{14}{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3A & =-\frac{5}{3}+\frac{14}{3} \\ 3A & =3 \\ A & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting back into $2A+B=\dfrac{14}{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(1)+B & =\frac{14}{3} \\ B & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{9x^2+2x-1}{(3x-1)^3} = \dfrac{1}{(3x-1)} +\dfrac{8}{3(3x-1)^2} + \dfrac{2}{3(3x-1)^3}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{9{x}^{2}+2x-1}{(3x-1)^{3}}\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{(3x-1)}+\frac{8}{3(3x-1)^{2}}+\frac{2}{3(3x-1)^{3}})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{3x-1}\text{d}x+\frac{8}{3}\int \frac{1}{(3x-1)^{2}}\text{d}x+\frac{2}{3}\int \frac{1}{(3x-1)^{3}}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x-1|+\frac{8}{3}(-\,\frac{1}{3(3x-1)})+\frac{2}{3}(-\,\frac{1}{6(3x-1)^{2}})+K \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x-1|-\frac{8}{9(3x-1)}-\frac{1}{9(3x-1)^{2}}+K\,.\end{aligned}
$$
